newsitem.title: INDIA: India still wants talks with Pakistan - agency.
newsitem.headline: India still wants talks with Pakistan - agency.

text.p: India wants to resume high-level peace talks with Pakistan despite Islamabad's apparent reluctance, Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral was quoted on Monday as saying.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) said Gujral told a seminar that an offer by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda in June to resume bilateral talks, suspended in early 1994, remained "despite a lack of enthusiasm in Islamabad's response".
Deve Gowda made the offer to restart talks at the senior Foreign Ministry level shortly after assuming power in June.
The talks were suspended in January 1994 after bogging down, primarily over Kashmir.
Pakistan wants Kashmiris to have the chance to vote in a plebiscite to determine their future. India, which rules over two thirds of the Himalayan region, says the issue is strictly internal.

In hard-hitting comments recently at the United Nations, Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto called elections in India's Jammu and Kashmir state a sham, and said New Delhi was preparing to deploy nuclear-capable missiles.
PTI quoted Gujral as telling the seminar in New Delhi that despite Bhutto's tough rhetoric, India would unilaterally take more measures to improve relations with its neighbour.
India recently eased visa procedures for Pakistani nationals to encourage greater cross-border contact.
Gujral said India was following a two-track policy towards Pakistan aimed at ending a "polemical war" over bilateral issues and encouraging contact between citizens of the two long-time rivals.

"Fifty percent of the energy of India's foreign office is being wasted in framing a policy towards Pakistan," said Gujral, who recently raised eyebrows when he avoided any mention of Pakistan in a speech to the U.N. General Assembly.
Diplomats said Gujral had purposely avoided a verbal duel with Bhutto at the U.N. meeting in New York as part of a broader effort to ease tension between the two countries.
